_meta.indication: ARCALYST (rilonacept) is an interleukin-1 blocker indicated for the treatment of Cryopyrin-Associated Periodic Syndromes (CAPS), including Familial Cold Autoinflammatory Syndrome (FCAS) and Muckle-Wells Syndrome (MWS) in adults and children 12 and older.

pivotal_trials.phase: Pivotal trial; CAPS is an orphan disease with too few patients for two independent randomized trials, so one pivotal trial was performed.
pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center study with a six-week double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled treatment period (Part A), followed by a nine-week single-blind active-treatment period and a nine-week double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized withdrawal phase (Part B).
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with FCAS and MWS forms of CAPS, genotype positive for CAPS.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to endpoint in the mean Key Symptom Score (KSS), derived from a daily diary rating five signs/symptoms of CAPS (joint pain, rash, feeling of fever/chills, eye redness/pain, fatigue) each on a 0–10 scale.
pivotal_trials.n: 47 CAPS patients in the pivotal trial (Part A: 23 rilonacept, 24 placebo).
pivotal_trials.result: Part A LS mean change in KSS was -2.4 (rilonacept) vs -0.5 (placebo), by-treatment difference -1.9 (95% CI -2.4, -1.3), p<0.0001; Part B LS mean change 0.1 vs 0.9, difference -0.8 (95% CI -1.3, -0.4), p=0.0002.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions are injection-site reactions and upper respiratory tract infections. Injection-site reactions occurred in 48% (Part A) and 36% (Part B withdrawal) of rilonacept patients vs 13% placebo. Infections risk is a class effect of IL-1 antagonism; coadministration with TNF blockers should be avoided.
target_moa: Rilonacept is a dimeric fusion protein of the extracellular domains of the IL-1 Type I receptor and IL-1 receptor accessory protein fused to the Fc portion of human IgG1; it binds IL-1 and interferes with its interaction with the receptor, countering the uncontrolled overproduction of IL-1 that drives inflammation in CAPS.

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not presented to an advisory committee; there are few CAPS experts and, given the short Priority review timeline, the Agency review team was determined to have the necessary expertise.

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for the new indication: maintenance of remission of Deficiency of Interleukin-1 Receptor Antagonist (DIRA) in adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 10 kg.

description.text: Added indication for treatment of recurrent pericarditis and reduction in risk of recurrence in adults and children 12 years and older

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for the treatment of recurrent pericarditis (RP) and reduction in risk of recurrence in adults and children 12 years and older.

basis.text: The Division granted the development program fast track designation; CAPS patients have increased morbidity with severe impairment in activities of daily living and the drug demonstrated marked improvement in open-label studies.

citations.quote: The Division granted the development program fast track designation. CAPS patients have increased morbidity defined as severe impairment in patients' activities of daily living. The drug in open-label studies demonstrated marked improvement in physical symptoms and laboratory parameters. Anakinra, an IL-1 antagonist, has also shown clinical activity in CAPS patients. orphan_indication.text: The Agency granted CAPS orphan designation; CAPS is a rare disease with approximately 200 to 300 affected patients in the US.

citations.quote: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. has submitted this BLA in support of approval of Arcalyst (rilonacept) for the treatment of Cryopyrin-Associated Periodic Syndromes (CAPS). CAPS is a rare disease with approximately 200 to 300 affected patients in the US. The Agency granted CAPS orphan designation. summary.text: Arcalyst (rilonacept) received orphan designation and fast track designation for CAPS, was reviewed under Priority review, and was approved February 27, 2008 based on a single pivotal placebo-controlled trial (IL1T-AI-0505) given the rarity of the disease; it was not referred to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: The Agency granted CAPS orphan designation.
The Division granted the development program fast track designation.
This application was not presented to an advisory committee.

requirement.text: Nonclinical: conduct a study in cynomolgus monkeys examining the effects of rilonacept exposure of the pregnant female during the third trimester of development.

citations.quote: 1. To conduct a study in cynomolgus monkeys examining the effects of rilonacept exposure of the pregnant female during the third trimester of development. You will submit a detailed outline of the study and rationale for review.

requirement.text: Nonclinical: conduct a juvenile animal study in cynomolgus monkeys to assess effects on sex hormones and bone development.

citations.quote: 2. To conduct a juvenile animal study in cynomolgus monkeys to assess effects on sex hormones and bone development. You will submit a detailed outline of the study and rationale for review.

requirement.text: Clinical: assess the safety of long-term use of rilonacept in the pediatric population by establishing a pediatric registry (duration at least five years) collecting growth, development, and adverse events including serious infections.

citations.quote: 3. To assess the safety of long-term use of rilonacept in the pediatric patient population by establishing a pediatric registry. The registry will collect information on growth and development as well as adverse events, particularly serious infections. The duration of the study will be at least five years.

requirement.text: Clinical: conduct a pharmacokinetics (PK) study in the pediatric population.

citations.quote: 4. To conduct a pharmacokinetics (PK) study in the pediatric population.

requirement.text: Clinical: assess whether lower maintenance doses or a longer interval between doses could be equally effective as, but potentially safer than, the approved dose.

citations.quote: 5. To assess whether either lower maintenance doses or a longer interval between doses could be equally effective as, but potentially safer than, the approved dose. The study could be designed to randomize patients on rilonacept to blindly continue on the approved dose or to switch to a lower dose or a longer interval between doses and to assess symptom scores over, for example, 9 weeks.

requirement.text: Pharmacovigilance: for the first five years of marketing, particular attention to reports of serious infections, pregnancy outcomes, and off-label use.

citations.quote: 1. Pharmacovigilance: In addition to standard pharmacovigilance practices, for the first five years of marketing, particular attention will focus on reports of serious infections, pregnancy outcomes, and off-label use.
